producer_report.summary:
The generator now fixes the sorting, ordering and repeated-source problems for any study, and the study data supplies the missing definitions and card titles. `cargo test --locked`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, clippy and the site generator all pass. I did not read the generated page itself; the new tests check its HTML.

**Generator (`xtask/src/site.rs`)**
- The Glossary is sorted case-insensitively by term.
- Claims are listed in numeric order of their id (c33 before c34, c9 before c10).
- A claim lists each source location (path and lines) once, so c2, c14 and c42 are fixed. These fixes are in the generator, so they hold for any study.
- "Start here" has a new "Words used first" list, read from `start_terms` in `intro.json`. It sits before "What firstmate is", so every term is defined before use. It has its own lead-in, `leadins.terms`.
- Each design-choice card shows its id and a title, read from `rationale_titles` in `intro.json`. A rationale with no title is an error.
- The lede now explains the study id: it is the name of the folder under `studies/` that holds the data the page is generated from.

**Study data and changelog**
- `intro.json` defines captain, yolo, green, red, local-only landing and home in "Words used first". It gives the six card titles, and the Glossary gains green, red and home.
- `CHANGELOG.md` has a new entry under Changed.
- The title field lives in `intro.json` because the rationale record type rejects unknown fields; adding `title` to `rationales.json` would have broken the study validation tests. The same reason applies to the two remaining study files.
- I left `rationales.json`, `claims.json`, `model.json` and `findings.json` unedited, although the brief lists them as deliverables. Nothing needed changing there, and `validation.json` stays consistent.

**Tests added in `xtask/src/site.rs`**
- The Glossary is sorted, with a fixture whose data order is unsorted, and the real Glossary contains green, red and home.
- Claims are in numeric order and no source repeats, checked on a fixture and on the real page.
- The real page gives each of ra1–ra6 a title and defines the Start-here terms before "What firstmate is".
- A rationale with no title is an error.
- I updated two existing tests. The lead-in count is now 5, and the uncited-intro test points at glossary index 0 instead of 1. I also added the new `start_terms` and `terms` lead-in paths to it.

**Words not defined by the source:** the study has no source defining "green". I defined it as a PR that is not red, citing c26 and c28. Red follows c28: a failing PR, or one with a required check that has not reported.

checks_run.note: All crates passed on the final run (exit 0). My first full run failed on one stale xtask test, an_uncited_intro_element_is_an_error; I fixed it and reran.
Wrote index.html, so the study still loads and validates. The new tests check the rendered HTML.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo test: the new generator tests pass, covering Glossary sorted alphabetically, no claim listing the same source twice, and claims in numeric order (c33 before c34).
Run cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check: both clean.
criteria_check.evidence: Both commands exited 0 with no warnings.

criteria_check.criterion: In the generated page, captain, yolo, green, red and local-only landing are defined at first use in 'Start here' or link to Glossary entries; the Glossary has entries for green, red and home.
criteria_check.evidence: The new 'Words used first' list defines them before 'What firstmate is'. The test the_real_page_titles_each_design_choice_and_defines_the_start_here_terms checks the order, and the Glossary test checks green, red and home.

criteria_check.criterion: Glossary entries render in alphabetical order, and claims render in numeric order with no claim showing a repeated source (c2, c14, c42 fixed).
criteria_check.evidence: The generator sorts the Glossary, orders claims by number and dedupes sources. The real-study tests assert all three on the rendered HTML.

criteria_check.criterion: Each design-choice card ra1–ra6 shows a short descriptive title alongside its id.
criteria_check.evidence: The card heading is now the id plus the title from rationale_titles. The test checks all six headings have a non-empty title.

criteria_check.criterion: The lede either explains the internal id firstmate-work-handling or no longer shows it unexplained.
criteria_check.evidence: The lede says the id is the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the page's data. A test asserts that sentence is on the page.

criteria_check.criterion: Run cargo run for the site generator xtask (as documented) and confirm the output page contains the new titles and definitions; the generator must still validate the study.
criteria_check.evidence: cargo run --locked -p xtask -- site wrote index.html. The real-study tests assert the new titles and definitions in the rendered HTML. I did not open the written file.

open_issues: rationales.json, claims.json, model.json and findings.json are listed as deliverables but I did not edit them; titles went to intro.json and the generator handles ordering and de-duplication.
The study has no source defining 'green'; the definition (a PR that is not red) is my inference from c26 and c28.
mistakes: My first test run failed because the uncited-intro test used glossary index 1 after I reordered the fixture. I fixed it.
learnings: The Rationale record in crates/athena-cap-study denies unknown fields, so rationale titles cannot go in rationales.json without a schema change; xtask reads free-form intro.json instead.
The site generator is run as `cargo run -p xtask -- site [--out dir]`, and its output defaults to target/site.
claims.json lists c34 before c33. The generator now sorts, so the file order is unchanged and harmless.
desires: Bash allowed tail or grep on tool output, so I could read a failing test's name from a long cargo test run without rerunning it.
